Higashimonzen. It is adjacent to {{ill|Jimoku-ji Temple|Q4160865|qid=Q4160865}}. There is a theory that identifies it with the “Nuribe Shrine” of {{ill|Ama District|Q685886|qid=Q685886|lt=Ama District}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Commendation Society|1987|pp=93–105}}. {{nihongo|'''Nuribe Shrine'''|漆部神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

== History ==
Until the {{ill|Early modern period|an|Edat Moderna|ar|الحقبة الحديثة المبكرة|ast|Edá Moderna|az|Erkən modern dövr|bar|Friae Neizeid|be|Ранні Новы час|bn|প্রারম্ভিক আধুনিক যুগ|br|Amzerioù modern|ca|Edat moderna|cs|Raný novověk|cy|Cyfnod Modern Cynnar|da|Tidlig moderne tid|de|Frühe Neuzeit|el|Πρώιμη νεότερη περίοδος|eo|Frua moderna epoko|es|Edad Moderna|et|Varauusaeg|eu|Aro Modernoa|fa|دوران نوین آغازین|fi|Varhaismoderni|fr|Époque moderne|gl|Idade Moderna|gn|Ára Ko'ãgagua|he|העת החדשה המוקדמת|hi|प्रारंभिक आधुनिक काल|hu|Korai újkor|ia|Etate Moderne|id|Periode modern awal|io|Modern-epoko|it|Età moderna|ja|近世|kbp|Alɩwaatʊ kɩfatʊ (Période moderne)|ko|근세|ku|Destpêka Dema Nûjen|kw|Oos Arnowydh A-Varr|lb|Neizäit|lfn|Eda moderna|li|Vreugmodernen Tied|lij|Etæ Modèrna|lld|Storia moderna|lmo|Età Modèrna|lo|ຍຸກ​ສະ​ໄຫມ​ຕົ້ນ​|lt|Naujieji amžiai|lv|Agrīnie jaunie laiki|mg|Andro Vaovao|mk|Ран нов век|new|प्रारम्भिक आधुनिक काल|nl|Vroegmoderne tijd|nn|Tidleg nytid|no|Tidlig moderne tid|oc|Edat Modèrna|pap|Edad Moderno|pcd|Histoère modérne|pl|Nowożytność|ps|لومړۍ معاصره دوره|pt|Idade Moderna|rm|Temp modern tempriv|ro|Epoca modernă timpurie|ru|Раннее Новое время|sc|Edade moderna|sh|Rani novi vijek|simple|Early modern period|sq|Periudha e hershme moderne|sr|Rani novi vek|stq|Eermodärne Tied|sv|Tidigmoderna tiden|th|สมัยใหม่ตอนต้น|tl|Makabagong kasaysayan|tr|Yeni Çağ|tt|Иртә яңа заман|uk|Ранній новий період|vi|Thời kỳ cận đại|vls|Nieuwn tyd|wuu|近世|yi|נייע צייט|zh|近世|zh_yue|近代史|qid=Q5308718}}, it was called '''Hachidai Myōjin''' and served as the tutelary shrine of Jimokuji Temple. Today, due to the {{ill|Shinbutsu bunri|Q1970535|qid=Q1970535}}, the precincts are divided.

The date of foundation is unknown. The oldest record is a {{ill|komonjo|Q89298567|qid=Q89298567}} from {{ill|Meiō|Q1193841|qid=Q1193841}} 7 (1498), in which eight divine names—“Kamo, Sumiyoshi, Kasuga, Hirano, Gion, Matsuo, Kibune, Inari”—and their {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=honji}} are written in ink{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Commendation Society|1987|pp=93–105}}. Records from the {{ill|Edo period|ar|فترة إيدو|ast|Periodu Edo|az|Edo dövrü|bcl|Panahon nin Edo|be|Перыяд Эда|bg|Едо (период)|bn|এদো যুগ|bo|ཨེ་དོའི་དུས་སྐབས།|br|Marevezh Edo|ca|Període Edo|ckb|سەردەمی ئێدۆ|cs|Období Edo|cv|Эдо тапхăрĕ|da|Edo-perioden|de|Edo-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Edo|es|Período Edo|et|Edo ajastu|eu|Edo aroa|fa|دوره ادو|fi|Edo-kausi|fr|Époque d'Edo|gl|Período Edo|he|תקופת אדו|hi|एदो अवधी|hr|Edo (razdoblje)|hu|Edo-kor|id|Zaman Edo|is|Jedótímabilið|it|Periodo Edo|ja|江戸時代|jv|Jaman Édo|ko|에도 시대|lt|Edo laikotarpis|lv|Edo periods|mk|Едо (период)|mn|Эдогийн эрин|ms|Zaman Edo|nl|Edoperiode|nn|Edotida|oc|Periòde Edo|pl|Edo (okres)|pt|Período Edo|ro|Perioada Edo|ru|Период Эдо|simple|Edo period|sk|Obdobie Edo|sl|Obdobje Edo|sq|Periudha Edo|sr|Едо период|su|Période Edo|sv|Edoperioden|th|ยุคเอโดะ|tl|Panahong Edo|tok|tenpo pi kulupu lawa Eto|tr|Edo Dönemi|uk|Період Едо|ur|ایڈو دور|uz|Edo davri|vi|Thời kỳ Edo|war|Panahon Edo|wuu|江戶時代|zh|江户时代|zh_min_nan|Edo sî-tāi|zh_yue|江戶時代|qid=Q184963|lt=Edo period}} state that 20 koku from the Jimokuji estate were allocated as ritual funds for this shrine. Several {{ill|Munafuda|Q8008834|qid=Q8008834}} (ridge tags) from the Edo to Shōwa periods survive, suggesting that the shrine buildings were repaired multiple times.

In the mid-Edo period, a theory was proposed identifying this shrine with the “Nuribe Shrine” of Ama District listed in the Engishiki Jinmyōchō. The basis for this identification was the presence nearby of a mound called Urushi-zuka (lacquer mound){{Sfn|Shikinaisha Commendation Society|1987|pp=93–105}}. However, there is no conclusive evidence for this identification, and {{ill|Tsuda Masanari|Q22123474|qid=Q22123474}}, who once identified this shrine as Nuribe Shrine, later refuted his own theory{{Sfn|Yahagi Village History Compilation Committee|2000|pp=750–755}}. Other candidate shrines for Nuribe Shrine include Ichigami Shrine in {{ill|Tsushima, Aichi|Q816736|qid=Q816736}} and Asama Shrine in {{ill|Nakagawa-ku, Nagoya|Q1155226|qid=Q1155226}}, {{ill|Shimonoisshiki-chō|Q62017174|qid=Q62017174|lt=Shimoisshiki-chō}}, among others. Scholarly opinion had not settled on an identification, as works such as the “Owari Province Shikisha Zadokumoku” state “Nuribe Shrine: location unknown”{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Commendation Society|1987|pp=93–105}}. The {{ill|Tokusen Jinmyōchō|Q11571092|qid=Q11571092}} considers the Engishiki shrine “Nuribe Shrine” of Ama District as follows:
{{Quotation|At present, considering Shiokiri, one might suspect this shrine to be Tsushima Shrine; another theory says it is Tsushima Ichigami Shrine, but there is no further proof. There is also a theory that it is Hachiman Shrine of Ninoe Village in the same district, suggesting that “Ninoe” might be read as “Nuribe,” but this is doubtful. Another claim says that the priests who served the Mitarai River of Asama Shrine in Shimoisshiki Village of Aichi District were connected to the Nuribe River, but investigation shows that this has been separated since ancient times and is not persuasive. There is also a theory that Jimokuji Kannon is a transformed form of this shrine, but this too lacks evidence and cannot be accepted. At present, it should be considered an abolished shrine.|“Tokusen Shinmeichō,” Owari Province, Ama District}}

Thus, there was also a theory that the Engishiki Nuribe Shrine had become an abolished shrine{{Sfn|Shikinaisha Commendation Society|1987|pp=93–105}}. However, because the theory that this shrine attached to Jimokuji was the Engishiki Nuribe Shrine spread from the Edo period onward, it was officially renamed Nuribe Shrine in {{ill|1957|Q5311|qid=Q5311}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 32).

In recent years, another theory has been proposed that Nuribe Myōjin was enshrined at an Ebisu Shrine that once existed in {{ill|Aisai|Q269644|qid=Q269644}}, {{ill|Kawakita-chō|Q131900621|qid=Q131900621|lt=Kawakita-chō}}{{Sfn|Yahagi Village History Compilation Committee|2000|pp=750–755}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
* Mimishukune
** Said to be the fifth generation descendant of {{ill|Amenohoakari|Q10940411|qid=Q10940411|lt=Honoakari-no-Mikoto}}. He is the ancestral deity of the Nuribe (people engaged in the production of lacquerware).
* {{ill|Konohanasakuya-hime|Q1781862|qid=Q1781862|lt=Konohana-sakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}}
* Hachidai Myōjin (a collective term for the deities of {{ill|Inari shrine|Q514480|qid=Q514480}}, {{ill|Kamo shrines|Q1306606|qid=Q1306606}}, {{ill|Kasuga Shrines|Q10855011|qid=Q10855011}}, {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|qid=Q11381857}}, {{ill|Gion shrines|Q11588442|qid=Q11588442}}, {{ill|Kifune Shrine|Q276779|qid=Q276779}}, {{ill|Hirano Shrine|Q738971|qid=Q738971}}, and {{ill|Matsuo shrine|Q11529677|qid=Q11529677}})

== Location ==
* 11 Higashimonzen, Jimokuji, Ama City, Aichi Prefecture
